title: Ideal multiplication for a principal quotient has the scalar image
statement: Let A be any commutative ring, f:X -> Spec(A) a scheme morphism, F any O_X-module, and pi any element of A. Let i be the base change of Spec(A/(pi)) -> Spec(A) to X, put J=i.ker [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], let m:J tensor F -> F be its ideal action [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and let mu:F -> F multiply by the image of pi under A -> Gamma(X,O_X). There exists an isomorphism e:image(mu) -> image(m) whose composite with the image inclusion of m equals the image inclusion of mu. This is an equality of image subobjects, with no claim that mu is mono or that either image inclusion is a kernel of a restriction unit.

source.place: Lemma 37.33.3, divisibility step; the ideal-action description uses Modules, Lemma 17.13.4 (Tag 08KS).

proof.text: Construct the structure-module stalk isomorphism from preservesColimitIso for the forgetful functor from commutative rings to abelian groups. Its germ formula follows from ι_preservesColimitIso_inv, and germ_smul proves linearity. For q = Spec(A -> A/(pi)), ΓSpecIso_naturality, RingHom.ker_equiv_comp and Ideal.mk_ker identify ker(q.appTop) with the image of span{pi} under ΓSpecIso.inv. ker_fst_of_isClosedImmersion, ideal_comap_appLE and Ideal.map_span then show on every affine U that i.ker.ideal U is generated by the restriction of r.

Represent an ideal-module germ on an affine neighbourhood using exists_mem_germ_eq_of_isBasis. range_toModulesι_app and the affine principal-ideal formula express its image as a multiple of r restricted to U, hence its ring germ is a multiple of r_x. Conversely r restricted to any affine neighbourhood belongs to the principal ideal and lifts along toModulesι; its germ gives r_x in the stalk image ideal. Ideal.span_le gives the reverse inclusion. Thus the ideal inclusion has stalk range span{r_x}.

Apply stalk_tensor_multiplication_range to the ideal inclusion and the structure-module stalk isomorphism. Substitute span{r_x} for the stalk ideal, and use Submodule.ideal_span_singleton_smul to obtain r_x times the top submodule. Represent each F germ by a section; stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply, smulHom_app_apply and germ_smul identify the stalk scalar map with multiplication by r_x. mem_smul_pointwise_iff_exists identifies its range with the same submodule.

For maps a and b with equal stalk ranges, the composite a with cokernel.π b vanishes on each stalk: every stalk image of a is a stalk image of b and the latter composite is zero by cokernel.condition and functoriality. Stalk-map germ compatibility and TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext imply that this composite is zero as a sheaf map; no stalk exactness theorem is required. Reverse the argument for b and a. Cancel the epi factorThruImage a to show image.ι a annihilates cokernel.π b, and use kernel.lift followed by Abelian.imageIsoImage b to obtain image a -> image b over F. Construct the reverse map similarly. Cancel the mono image inclusions to show the composites are identities. These maps form the required isomorphism and compatibility equation.

proof_origin.place: Divisibility step and Tag 08KS ideal action; T1 formal proof via affine quotient ideals, the proved stalk tensor range theorem, and categorical kernel-of-cokernel lifts, avoiding the previous stalk-exactness and gluing route.

lean.statement:
theorem principal_quotient_multiplication_image
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) (F : X.Modules) (π : A) :
    let i := pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {π}))))
    let m := i.ker.toModulesι ▷ F ≫ (λ_ F).hom
    let μ := F.smulHom (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom π)
    ∃ e : image μ ≅ image m, e.hom ≫ image.ι m = image.ι μ
